skill.name: global-tech-stack
skill.description: Guide AI coding agents to follow project-specific technology choices for frameworks, databases, testing, authentication, deployment, and third-party services.
skill.summary: Apply project technology standards before adding tools, dependencies, integrations, or architecture changes.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The skill contains one confirmed filesystem concern because it instructs the agent to follow a parent-directory relative link outside the skill folder. The system reconnaissance finding is a false positive because the description is normal technology-stack guidance.

remediation.issue: The skill references a file outside its own package using a parent-directory path.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the tech-stack guidance inside the skill package or replace the link with a safe marketplace-supported reference.

static_findings.snippet: description: Understand and apply project-specific technology choices including frameworks, language

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 29 links to ../../../agent-os/standards/global/tech-stack.md, which directs the agent outside the skill package. This creates unexpected filesystem access and should be packaged safely.
Line 3 describes project technology-stack guidance and does not ask the agent to enumerate host systems, secrets, users, or network details. The wording is operational context, not reconnaissance.

high_findings.title: Path traversal sequence
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 29 links to ../../../agent-os/standards/global/tech-stack.md, which directs the agent outside the skill package. This creates unexpected filesystem access and should be packaged safely.

content.value_statement: Teams lose consistency when AI agents choose new frameworks or dependencies without project context. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to follow existing stack decisions.
actual_capabilities: Identify when technology choices need project-specific standards before coding.
Encourage consistent framework, package, ORM, testing, and deployment decisions.
Prompt agents to consult a shared tech-stack reference before adding dependencies.
Support onboarding by documenting when stack guidance applies.
Reduce conflicting tools during refactors or third-party integrations.
limitations: Does not include the actual global tech-stack content inside the skill file.
Relies on a relative link that may not exist after marketplace installation.
Does not validate dependencies, licenses, vulnerabilities, or runtime compatibility.
Provides guidance only; it does not enforce architecture automatically.

use_cases.title: Standardize Dependency Choices
use_cases.description: Review proposed packages against the project stack before adding new libraries or frameworks.

use_cases.title: Build Within Existing Patterns
use_cases.description: Use approved frameworks, testing tools, databases, and service patterns while implementing a feature.

use_cases.title: Learn Stack Boundaries
use_cases.description: Understand which technology decisions are already defined before making project changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Stack Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review whether my planned dependency matches the project tech stack before I add it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before adding a dependency

prompt_templates.title: Implement Feature Consistently
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill while planning a feature that touches the database, test setup, and framework conventions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Feature work across established stack layers

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate whether this architecture change introduces tools that conflict with existing standards.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Cross-Service Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a third-party service integration and list stack assumptions, approved tools, and risks.

output_examples.input: I want to add a new payment provider and background job tool.
output_examples.output: The response should identify existing integration patterns, confirm approved service categories, and flag any new runtime or deployment requirements.

output_examples.input: Review this database library choice before implementation.
output_examples.output: The response should compare the choice with the project's ORM guidance, migration approach, testing needs, and operational constraints.

output_examples.input: Help onboard a developer to the project stack.
output_examples.output: The response should summarize where stack decisions apply and which changes need review before implementation.

best_practices: Keep the referenced tech-stack document current and versioned with the project.
Ask the agent to explain stack assumptions before adding new dependencies.
Use this skill before architecture, database, authentication, and integration changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to bypass security, license, or dependency review.
Do not introduce a new framework only because a prompt requests it.
Do not rely on a missing external tech-stack document in a published skill.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents follow project-specific technology choices when planning or changing code.

faq.question: Does it choose the best framework automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides decisions toward documented project standards and still needs human review.

faq.question: Can it validate dependency security?
faq.answer: No. Use separate security, license, and vulnerability checks for dependency approval.

faq.question: Why is the external link a concern?
faq.answer: The skill points outside its package, which can break installation and create unexpected filesystem access.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, technical leads, and onboarding team members can use it before technology or architecture changes.
